title: Te quiero
desc: Two words for one thing, and the bigger one said first
setting: You are on the phone with Lucía at night and she has just said something soft.

steps.speaker: Lucía
steps.es: Me gusta cuando hablás así, gordo.
steps.en: I like it when you talk like that, gordo.

options.feedback: Te quiero is the everyday one and it is the one people actually say. It is not the small version, whatever the dictionary suggests.
Safe. She left you an opening the size of a door and you stood in it.
Te amo is enormous here and belongs in songs. A lot of Nicaraguans go a whole life without saying it once, and she has gone quiet.

steps.speaker: Lucía
steps.es: Ideay. ¿Y por qué me decís así de repente?
steps.en: Ideay. And why are you saying that all of a sudden?

options.es: Porque de verdad lo pienso. Nada más.
options.en: Because I really do mean it. Nothing more.
options.feedback: Plain and short. Explaining it further would make it into a speech, and a speech is not what she asked for.

options.en: Sorry, did I say it too soon?
options.feedback: Honest. Apologising for it half takes it back, and she was not asking for an apology.

options.es: Así se dice en mi país.
options.en: That is how we say it where I am from.
options.feedback: You have turned a moment into a translation problem. She was not asking about your country.

steps.speaker: Lucía
steps.es: Es que aquí eso casi no se dice. Mi papá nunca se lo dijo a mi mamá.
steps.en: It is just that here that is hardly ever said. My father never said it to my mother.

options.en: And how did she know, then?
options.feedback: The right question, and the answer is everything else: who cooks, who waits up, who is still there. Words are not the main channel here.
She was not telling you a sad story. She was telling you how her parents' marriage worked.

options.es: Entonces yo se lo voy a decir siempre.
options.en: Then I will say it to you always.
options.feedback: Sweet, and it talks over what she just told you about her own house.

steps.speaker: Lucía
steps.es: Yo también te quiero, tonto. Pero decímelo despacio.
steps.en: I love you too, silly. But say it to me slowly.

options.en: All right then. I love you, Lucía.
options.feedback: She asked for the smaller word said properly, and she gave you hers first. Do exactly what she asked.
She just said it back to you. That deserved more than two words.
It was not an instruction about speed. Asking her to explain it is the surest way to end the evening.
